_comment: NOT MODEL OUTPUT. Hand-written to demonstrate the tool loop without an API key. Replaying this stores source='replay-scripted'. Re-record with: python -m diagnose --record

content.thinking: Checkout is returning 500s. Before guessing at a cause I want the actual error lines, so I know whether this is a crash or a handled failure path.
Unhandled exceptions on POST /checkout, so something is raising rather than returning an error response. Next: what changed recently.

The newest commit claims to be a perf change to checkout's price lookup. That subject is plausible enough to be innocent, so I should not take it at face value — blame the checkout body and see which commit actually owns those lines.
Blame confirms the lookup lines belong to that commit. Now read the precomputed table definition and the validation check together — the bug is likely in how the two relate.

content.text: Found it. The validation set and the price table disagree on key type.

input.root_cause: PRICE_CENTS_BY_ID is built with str(p["id"]) as its keys, while validation checks the incoming product_id against KNOWN_IDS, which holds the raw ints. A request with a valid integer id therefore passes validation and then misses the price table, raising KeyError. Because the miss happens after validation succeeds, every well-formed checkout fails with an unhandled 500 rather than a 4xx.
input.rationale: Key the price table by the same type validation checks against, so a value that passes KNOWN_IDS cannot miss PRICE_CENTS_BY_ID. Fixing the key type addresses the mismatch itself; coercing at the call site or catching KeyError would only hide it while leaving the two structures disagreeing.
